title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Working Out the Open Balance Ceiling at Review
content:
The open balance ceiling written on a rate program at review is worked out from the account's own record
of demand service work and payment over a review window, and it replaces the ceiling the program
carried. The record is read over the last 12 months. The starting ceiling is the tier's published credit
limit, the figure published for the program the account holds under the Demand Service Rate Programs. No
step is added for the account's payment record. Nothing is cut for arrears. No step is added for the
owner's other accounts with the company. No allowance is added for the account's call volume. The
ceiling is the starting ceiling multiplied once by one plus the payment record step plus the portfolio
step less the arrears cut, the three steps being combined into a single factor and never applied one
after another, with the volume allowance added to that product afterwards rather than multiplied by it,
and only the total is rounded, to the nearest cent, half up.

## The order of the assembly

1. The starting ceiling stands at the tier's published credit limit.
2. The payment record step, the portfolio step and the arrears cut are combined into one factor: one
   plus the payment record step plus the portfolio step, less the arrears cut.
3. The starting ceiling is multiplied once by that single factor. The three never act one after another.
4. The volume allowance is added to that product, never multiplied by it.
5. Only the total is rounded, to the nearest cent, half up.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

A rate program whose published credit limit is 25000 US dollars comes to review. The starting ceiling is
25000 US dollars. No step is added for the payment record and none for the owner's other accounts, and
nothing is cut for arrears, so the single factor is one. 25000 US dollars multiplied once by one is
25000 US dollars, and no allowance is added for call volume. Rounded to the nearest cent, half up, the
ceiling written on the program is 25000.00 US dollars, replacing the ceiling the program carried.
